sessions.title: First class · A place to recommend

tips.문장 구조: Part 3: answer → reason → example → answer again.

focus.1: Don't use is + another verb (is come ✗). Singular subject → has. Feelings: confused, not confusing. Part 3: answer → reason → example → answer again.

cards.en: I come from Seoul. / I'm from Seoul.
cards.gram: Don't use is/am together with another verb like come. Say I come from or I'm from. For the continuous form, use is coming from.

cards.en: My city has to improve its public transport.
cards.gram: My city is singular, so use has to. Only I / you / we / they take have to.
cards.wrong: My city have to improve public transport.

cards.gram: Use -ed for how you feel (confused). Use -ing for the thing that causes the feeling: The question is confusing. "I'm confusing" means you confuse other people.
Different is an adjective; the noun is difference. More than one → There are + plural noun (differences).
Every is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb: Every city has its own charm.

cards.en: Use a range of linking words instead.
cards.gram: Try not to repeat just like. Use for example, such as, similar to, or in the same way.

words.ko: confused = how you feel; confusing = the thing that causes it
words.ex: The question was confusing, so I was confused.
There is a big difference between the two cities.

words.ko: invent a story (it's OK in the test)
words.ex: If you don't know, you can make up a story.

words.ko: support your answer with a reason
words.ex: Back up your answer with a reason.

words.ko: a useful pattern for giving reasons
words.ex: The reason why I like Busan is that it's near the sea.
